prompt: For a finite nonempty simple graph $G$, which parameter is the minimum number of labels needed to build $G$ using labelled single vertices, disjoint union, complete joins between two distinct labels, and global relabelling?

answers.explanation: Labels are reusable construction states. The parameter counts how many labels suffice for an expression, not the size of a clique.
Clique number is the size of a largest complete subgraph; it does not count construction labels.
Construction labels need not form independent sets and are not a proper colouring.
Twin-width is measured by red degrees along contractions.
Treewidth counts bag size minus one in a tree decomposition.
Shrubdepth also constrains depth through a tree-model; unrestricted expression height is allowed here.
Construction labels can be reused and changed; final twin classes need not correspond to one fixed global labelling.
Linear clique-width additionally restricts disjoint union so that only one vertex is added at a time.
NLC-width uses a different join-and-union operation, with edges added between the two operands according to a label-pair relation.
Rank-width uses binary adjacency-matrix ranks across cuts, rather than this expression syntax.

sources.title: Ganian et al. — Shrub-depth: Capturing Height of Dense Graphs, §§2–4
Bonnet et al. — Twin-width I, §§2–4 (2021 version)
